title: Tech Stocks Sink, AI Rally Dwindles As Powell Hints At Further Hikes: What's Driving Markets Wednesday
description:
The U.S. stock market fell on Wednesday, with tech stocks largely underperforming the rest of the market, as Fed Chair Jerome Powell signaled during testimony before the House Financial Services Committee that additional hikes may be forthcoming to bring inflation back to the Fed’s target.
Nearly all FOMC participants anticipated it would be reasonable to raise interest rates somewhat more by year’s end, Powell said, stressing that the decision to pause hikes doesn’t mean the end of tightening. 
The market slide was spurred by the negative performance from tech titans, with Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA), Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Netflix Inc. (NASDAQ:NFLX) down 4.5%, 2.4% and 2.3%, respectively.
FedEx Corp. (NYSE:FDX) reported slightly better-than-anticipated earnings, but missed revenue estimates and provided disappointing guidance for the upcoming quarters.
Earlier in the day, markets negatively reacted to a hotter-than-expected U.K. inflation rate in May, which fueled expectations for more aggressive Bank of England rate hikes. 
Traders increased their expectations for a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike in July, from 62% last week to 79% today. This shift caused U.S. Treasury yields to move higher during the session. 
Cues From Wednesday’s Trading:
The S&P 500 Index fell 0.3%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index lost 170 points or 1.1% for the day. 
The Dow Jones Industrial Average held steady, while small caps in the Russell 2000 had a timid 0.1% drop.

title: BofA Analyst Cuts Price Target for AMD, Re-rates Semiconductor Companies, Expects Long-Term Stock Momentum For Sector
description:
BofA analyst Vivek Arya sees Q2 for U.S. semiconductor companies in line and modestly below Q3 on lukewarm macro, but CY24 EPS recovery could sustain longer-term stock momentum.
The analyst upgraded Camtek Ltd (NASDAQ: CAMT) to Buy and raised the price target to $50 from $30 on AI packaging momentum. It reflected increasing advanced packaging penetration and continued WFE outgrowth.
CAMT is a semiconductor manufacturing equipment supplier highly exposed to some of the fastest-growing end markets in the space, including advanced packaging (~60% of sales) and compound semiconductors (~15% of sales). 
Given increased exposure to the above growth markets, the analyst sees potential for multiple re-rating toward larger front-end peers.
Arya downgraded Coherent Corp (NYSE: COHR), raising the price target to $55 from $42 and MACOM Technology Solutions Holdings, Inc (NASDAQ: MTSI)

description:
Semiconductor stocks rallied sharply in 2023, with the sector among the best-performing S&P 500 sector classes. Against the backdrop, an analyst said on Tuesday he views the group as expensive on the 2024 estimates but remains positive about names levered to the “2nd Wave of AI.”
